data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Akamai, Robinhood and Nio among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the red on Friday, after traders and investors digested the latest jobs data, which came in stronger than forecasted.

Nasdaq (COMP:IND) rose 0.7% for the week, while the Dow (DJI) gained marginally. Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Robinhood raised to Overweight at Morgan Stanley

Morgan Stanley upgraded Robinhood Markets (HOOD) to Overweight from Equalweight as the financial app platform's broadening range of products drives growth in assets per customer, increased activity per customer, and greater economics captured per activity.

Morgan Stanley increased its price target for Robinhood stock to $150 from $124.

"Rather than relying primarily on funded-account growth or a stronger retail trading environment, HOOD increasingly has multiple ways to grow revenue from its 28M customers already on the platform," analyst Michael J. Cyprys wrote.

Akamai upgraded on Compute business gains

Akamai (AKAM) was upgraded to Overweight from Neutral by Piper Sandler due in part to recent wins from its Compute business segment.

"Akamai has yet to disclose its Compute megawatts that we expect will be given in time," said Piper Sandler analyst James Fish.

"Today, we estimate Akamai has approximately 22 active MWs out of about 47 MWs of capacity, though given $2.8B+ of commitments/35 MWs. Akamai is 'sold-out' already and needs more capacity to get these online. As such, we are raising our capex estimates to $2.3B in '27-'28 each, which assumes a rising capex/MW cost and about 30 active MWs/year incrementally."

Piper Sandler lowered its price target on the stock to $125 from $140.

Nio downgraded on ‘slower’ 2H growth

Nio (NIO) was downgraded to Hold from Buy by Freedom Broker, which cut its price target to $4 from $7, citing weaker-than-expected third-quarter guidance that could signal “slower growth in 2H26.”

Analyst Dmitriy Pozdnyakov expects third-quarter revenue of 31.5 billion yuan and deliveries of 108,000 vehicles. They cut its 2026 revenue forecast to 123 billion yuan from 138 billion yuan and delivery forecast to 419,000 vehicles from 468,000.

Pozdnyakov said NIO (NIO) continues to show “strong EV shipment growth” and is “actively expanding” its ONVO and FIREFLY brands. They expect rising volumes to support positive net income through “improved absorption of operating expenses.”

Ambarella (AMBA) was downgraded by investment firm Craig Hallum to Hold from Buy after the semiconductor design company's second-quarter results and guidance indicated a lack of clarity on a couple of key items. The brokerage cut price target to $70 from $95.

HSBC Global Investment Research downgraded Trip.com (TCOM) to Hold from Buy, citing regulatory pressures and expectations for a softer-than-expected travel season that could weigh on upcoming results.

data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: Nvidia, Dell, Broadcom in focus
data.description:
The tech sector remained in the spotlight this week as investors digested earnings reports from heavyweights including Dell (DELL) and Broadcom (AVGO).

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) closed in the red on Friday. For the week, the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) rose marginally during the week. The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the last week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

  • Sandisk (SNDK) +17.17%
  • Dell (DELL) +14.84%
  • Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) +12.51%
  • Micron Technology (MU) +8.85%
  • Intel (INTC) +7.07%

Top Losers:

  • Fair Isaac (FICO) -19.22%
  • Autodesk (ADSK) -16.40%
  • Ciena (CIEN) -15.16%
  • Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) -14.01%
  • Synopsys (SNPS) -11.02%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B

Nvidia (NVDA) confirmed prior media reports on Thursday when it announced it had agreed to purchase Hugging Face for $12.9B.

Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement. Nvidia compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face.

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

Dell soars 16% on record results; HPE raises guidance

Dell (DELL) shares were nearly 16% higher on Wednesday after the IT giant delivered a stronger-than-expected second quarter and sharply raised its fiscal 2027 outlook, underscoring the strength of demand for AI infrastructure.

Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan raised his price target to $600 from $505 and reiterated his Buy rating, stating that Dell is benefiting from the supply constraints facing the AI industry.

HPE's (HPE) third quarter 2026 results also featured momentum across all its business segments and an increase in its outlook.

Broadcom guidance for 2027, 2028 surprises Wall Street

Broadcom (AVGO) offered weaker-than-expected guidance that overshadowed its third-quarter results. Looking ahead, Broadcom said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to be approximately $34.8B, with adjusted EBITDA around 66%. Analysts had expected $35.1B in fourth-quarter sales, according to Bloomberg.

However, the company’s offering of guidance for 2028 surprised Wall Street. Following the results and guidance, several Wall Street firms raised their price targets on Broadcom, including Cantor Fitzgerald, which went to $600 from $525. Macquarie upgraded shares to Outperform and put a $490 price target on the stock.

Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore said that the guidance for 2027 shows Broadcom is on track, but the 2028 guidance was a positive surprise, even if there is some skepticism attached to it.

Other notable tech headlines include "Big Short" investor Michael Burry renewing his bearish view on Palantir (PLTR) and criticizing the company’s valuation, business model, accounting, stock-based compensation, and CEO Alex Karp’s aircraft-related expenses, among other things.

HP (HPQ) also posted Q3 results and guidance that topped Wall Street's estimates.

However, the company said looking ahead to the remainder of our fiscal year, it continues to expect input costs to rise, putting near-term pressure on its operating margins, particularly in Personal Systems. 

Apple (AAPL) is reportedly facing a £2B (~$2.7B) lawsuit in the UK over its app tracking practices, with lawyers for app developers alleging that the company used its position as a gatekeeper to give its own advertising business an advantage.

data.title: Banks, crypto in gainers; Aon, credit card stocks among losers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street closed the trading week mixed, as tech giant Broadcom posted its latest earnings in a week when yields and rates remained in focus after the latest nonfarm payrolls report landed.

"The real economy took a hit this week, an artifact of the better-than-expected jobs report released on Friday. The sell-off that followed was largely caused by the hawks, who see the good news as reasons for a rate hike," said Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman.

"The prospect of higher rates while inflation is primarily being driven by energy inflation means a squeeze on consumers and anything that lives off financing costs," said Bowman.

State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) closed the week flat at $58.10. However, bank stocks were gaining. The Invesco KBW Bank ETF (KBWB) added 1.42% week-over-week to $97.65.

Investors may consider banks with higher fee income components more attractive than traditional spread lenders, or institutions that derive at least two-thirds of their revenue from net interest income, according to Brean Capital analyst Christopher Marinac.

"There could be a perception or narrative that so-called 'fee banks' are better stocks for an uncertain period of Federal Reserve interest rate policy and debate over sustained [earnings-per-share] growth in the industry," Marinac wrote in a research report.

Among megacap stocks, the foreign stock Mitsubishi UFJ Financial (MUFG) led the gainers, potentially benefiting from a weaker dollar.

The stock added 5.20% from the prior week to close at $24.09.

With the U.S. Treasury Department's ongoing expanded bond buybacks, "it is reasonable to assume we could see some dollar weakness, and that could continue to kind of help support returns in international equities from a dollar-[based] investor standpoint," Josh Jones, portfolio manager at Boston Partners, told CNBC News.

The US Dollar Index (DXY) inched down ~0.5% during the week.

Payment stocks, Mastercard (MA) (-2.70% W/W to $579.21), American Express (AXP) (-2.11% W/W to $326.16), and Visa (V) (-1.71% W/W to $375.07), led the decliners as the stablecoin disruption saw a major development this week. A group of 21 international financial institutions announced plans to establish a new stablecoin company in the second half of 2026. 

The newly-created stablecoin is expected to launch in the first half of 2027.

The venture comes as a competition to Open Standard's Open USD (OPEN-USD) stablecoin that has signed over 140 companies to participate, including Visa (V), Mastercard (MA), and American Express (AXP).

Aon (AON) topped the largecap losers, retreating 9.09% week-over-week to $323.09.

The stock dropped 10% on Monday after the professional services and insurance brokerage firm announced a $17B acquisition of USI Insurance Services from KKR (KKR).

Crypto stocks, IREN (IREN) (+26.04% W/W to $44.68), Hut 8 (HUT) (+17.79% W/W to $93.55), Robinhood Markets (HOOD) (+17.12% W/W to $122.11), Circle Internet (CRCL) (+17.11% W/W to $102.05), and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) (+13.44% W/W to $26.33), were the biggest advancers as bitcoin (BTC-USD) added ~3% during the course of the week.

For Seeking Alpha analysts' thoughts on whether the cryptocurrency was finally making a comeback, click here.

Midcap stocks, Strive (ASST) (+24.84% W/W to $27.14) and Riot Platforms (RIOT) (+14.80% W/W to $21.80), stood out as winners in the category.

Goosehead Insurance (GSHD) was the top midcap loser, pulling back 8.49% to close at $65.21. The insurer reported insider transactions this week.

Among smallcap stocks, AlTi Global (ALTI) (-25.19% W/W to $3.00). TOP Financial (TOP) (-10.40% W/W to $14.99), Chaince Digital (CD) (+24.85% W/W to $4.07), and Bit Digital (BTBT) (+14.69% W/W to $1.64) were the notable movers.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: 7 of 8 key S&P 500 reporting firms top EPS estimates as all 8 post Y/Y profit growth
data.description:
Corporate earnings featured a notable lineup of reports from 8 key S&P 500 reporting firms across the information technology, health care, consumer discretionary, and consumer staples sectors.

Earnings Roundup:

  • Bottom Line: Earnings performance was exceptionally strong, as 7 out of 8 reporting companies beat consensus EPS estimates while 1 matched expectations in-line. All 8 companies achieved year-over-year profit expansion.

  • Top Line: Revenue performance was more mixed, with 5 companies exceeding Wall Street expectations and 3 falling short of consensus estimates. Overall, 7 of the 8 firms delivered year-over-year top-line growth.

 

 

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

Dell Technologies (DELL) jumped 15.81% after their fiscal second-quarter 2027 earnings exceeded expectations. They reported a 58% increase in revenue to $46.97 billion and an adjusted EPS of $7.04. The Infrastructure Solutions Group experienced an 89% increase, and the company projects third-quarter revenue of $49 billion and full-year sales of $192 billion, boosted by AI server demand.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) slipped 9.28% despite topping fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 expectations and issuing an optimistic forward forecast. Revenue jumped 34% year-over-year to $3.41 billion, driven by $2.67 billion in subscription and support revenue and $738 million in product sales, while adjusted EPS came in at $1.02, beating consensus estimates. For the first quarter, the cybersecurity leader projects revenue between $3.30 billion and $3.31 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.96 to $0.98, alongside strong growth targets for full-year fiscal 2027.

Medtronic (MDT) rose 1.53% post-earnings after reporting strong first-quarter results that exceeded Wall Street expectations. Revenue increased by 13.8% year-over-year to $9.76 billion, surpassing estimates by $220 million. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.45, beating consensus by $0.06. Cardiovascular revenue grew by 18.9%. Medtronic raised its full-year growth guidance to 7.25%-7.75% and adjusted its FY27 non-GAAP EPS outlook to $5.94–$6.00 (from $5.90–$6.00 previously) against a $5.95 consensus.

Broadcom (AVGO) dropped 2.7% post-earnings due to lower-than-expected revenue guidance for Q4, despite strong Q3 results. In Q3, adjusted EPS was $3.32, with revenue up 86% at $29.59 billion, boosted by strong semiconductor and infrastructure sales. Q4 revenue is expected around $34.8 billion, below analyst expectations.

Lululemon Athletica (LULU) shares dropped nearly 20% in post-market trading after the company lowered its full-year sales forecast due to declining sales in China and increased competition. Lululemon expects a 5% to 7% sales decline, estimating $10.35B to $10.50B, down from $11.0B to $11.50B. Current-quarter sales are projected to fall 10% to 11%. In the second quarter, revenue declined 4%, with comparable sales down 9%, despite an EPS of $2.92 exceeding estimates.

Brown-Forman (BF.A) (BF.B) rose 3.87% post-earnings after reporting mixed first-quarter results, with earnings per share rising 6% to $0.38, beating estimates. Gross margin increased due to lower costs. Sales were affected by weak tequila and barrel sales, the end of a distribution agreement, and declines in some markets, despite growth in ready-to-drink products. Management expects flat sales and a 3% to 5% decline in operating income for the full year.

NetApp (NTAP) gained 2.55% post-earnings after delivering a strong first-quarter results for fiscal 2027, with a 30% increase in revenue to $2.03 billion and adjusted EPS at $2.58, exceeding estimates. However, shares dropped 8% post-report due to a 35% decrease in free cash flow. The company provided strong guidance for Q2 and raised its full-year revenue and EPS forecasts.

Campbell's Company (CPB) saw a sharp decline in stock value, down 6.96%, after missing fourth-quarter revenue estimates, with net sales down 8% to $2.1 billion. Profit margins decreased significantly due to cost inflation, leading to a 25% drop in adjusted EBIT and a 37% decline in adjusted EPS. The board approved a 36% cut in the quarterly dividend and announced a cost-savings initiative targeting $500 million by FY30, while fiscal guidance also fell below expectations.

Earnings next week:

As earnings season rolls on, investors are tracking key reports across tech, consumer staples, healthcare, and industrials to gauge enterprise IT spending, consumer health, and broader economic demand.

Upcoming highlights include software powerhouses Adobe Inc. (ADBE) and Oracle Corporation (ORCL); consumer staples leaders Casey's General Stores (CASY) and The Kroger Co. (KR); along with key updates from healthcare provider The Cooper Companies, Inc. (COO) and industrial services firm Copart, Inc. (CPRT).

data.title: Hon Hai, a key partner for Nvidia, records 52% growth in August amid AI boom
data.description:
Hon Hai Precision Industry (HNHPF), a key server assembly partner for Nvidia (NVDA), reported NT$921.8B ($29.1B) in revenue for August on Saturday, marking its second-best monthly sales with 52% YoY growth, driven by accelerating AI momentum.

The Taiwan-based company, also known as Foxconn, added that its consolidated sales for the first eight months of the year reached NT$6.5T ($0.2T), indicating ~40% YoY growth. August marked its second-highest sales figure in history, trailing July when it added NT$946.51B ($29.9B) in revenue with a 54% YoY rise.

The company said that its cloud and networking division saw sizable year-on-year growth momentum amid accelerating AI demand, as did its electronics component and computing product divisions.

Hon Hai (HNHAF), which also serves as an iPhone assembler for Apple (AAPL), reported strong growth momentum in its smart consumer electronics division amid higher prices and as clients restocked inventory ahead of new product launches.

As for the outlook, Hon Hai (HNHAF) says Q3 is a peak season for the information and communications technology industry in general. Analysts on average expect the company to report a 37% rise in sales for the quarter, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Communication services sector rises in August; Paramount leads gains
data.description:
The communication services (XLC) gained nearly 3% in August despite broader market volatility as investors focused on earnings from companies including Paramount Skydance and Fox (FOXA).

Communication Services Sector August Scorecard

  • Sector Return: 2.97%
  • Best Performer: Paramount Skydance (+26.4%)
  • Worst Performer: Trade Desk (-28.3%)
  • Top Theme: Earnings reports

Top communication services performers of the quarter

On the individual front, Paramount Skydance (PSKY) was the biggest winner after the company showed improved profitability during its second-quarter results. The media giant said it continues to prepare for the combination with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) while staying focused on executing a standalone strategy and delivering strong results. Paramount was followed by Fox (FOXA) and AT&T (T), which gained over 12% during the month.

Seeking Alpha analyst Dividend Collection Agency, Contributing analyst to the iREIT+Hoya Capital investment group, believes that Paramount’s gain was mainly due to optimism regarding the settlement with the California attorney general to move the Warner Bros. (WBD) deal forward.

“The company also received backing from several cinemas supporting the deal and stated they were willing to sell their news business CNN to get the deal done,” the analyst added.

Here are the top five gainers of the month:

  • Paramount Skydance (PSKY) +27.5%
  • Fox (FOXA) +12.9%
  • AT&T (T) +12.6%
  • Netflix (NFLX) +10.4%
  • Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) +10.1%

Top communication services losers of the month:

On the other hand, Trade Desk (TTD) was the biggest detractor in August, slipping over 28% as investors reacted to the second-quarter earnings miss and signs of slowing momentum at the digital advertising platform. Earlier in the month, Susquehanna downgraded the stock to Neutral from Positive and cut its PT to $14 from $34, citing near-term execution challenges, weaker advertiser demand, and pressure on growth expectations.

AppLovin (APP) claimed the second spot, while Alphabet (GOOG) was third on the list.

Analyst Dividend Collection Agency said Trade Desk’s decline was also because margin contracted 500 basis points from 39% to 34% during the quarter, implying pressure on growth expectations and near-term execution challenges.

“AppLovin (APP) also saw a large decline, down 20%+. I believe this was mainly due to the significant increase in CAPEX, up a staggering 10,000% from the previous year. Although several companies have been aggressively spending to remain competitive in the AI race, the high inflationary environment, in my opinion, caused investors to become more short-sighted. The market seems to now have shifted to companies remaining more conservative with their spending instead of pursuing future long-term growth opportunities,” the analyst said.

Here are the top five detractors of the month:

  • Trade Desk (TTD) -28.13%
  • AppLovin (APP) -26.71%
  • Alphabet (GOOG) -11.64%
  • Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) -9.33%
  • Reddit (RDDT) -6.8%

data.title: Apple's 9-9 event 'most consequential iPhone launch' in decade as Ternus takes over: MS
data.description:
Apple's (AAPL) September 9 fall product launch event, "Surprise and Shine," might stand as its most significant in nearly a decade, according to the analysts at Morgan Stanley.

"Apple's 'Surprise and Shine' product launch event next Wednesday should follow a very similar format to past years—a 90-minute presentation of Apple's newest device introductions, namely the Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, AirPods 5, iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max, and, most importantly, its first foldable iPhone," said Morgan Stanley analysts, led by Erik Woodring, in an investor report.

"However, the event will prove to be anything but ordinary. This is because for the first time in 15 years, Tim Cook will not headline the event; instead, new CEO John Ternus will lead the company into its first major iPhone form factor change in nearly 10 years, unveiling the much-anticipated iPhone Fold (Ultra?), alongside what are likely to be the broadest and most significant, like-for-like iPhone price hikes in company history," he added.

If Apple's first foldable phone captures a positive reaction from consumers, it could contribute significantly to revenue for the December quarter.

"We currently forecast ~6.5M foldable iPhone shipments in the December quarter, translating to ~$14B of revenue, or 16% of total December quarter iPhone revenue," Woodring noted. "Beyond the near-term financial contribution, it will be worth watching how Apple leverages the larger form factor and whether it delivers use cases that are better on a foldable vs. simply a larger screen—and most importantly, how the device really feels in hand. If consumer reception is strong, we believe the category could ultimately become larger than current supply chain forecasts imply."

Another critical point to consider is how consumers will react to price hikes across the new iPhone lineup. Morgan Stanley expects like-for-like iPhone Pro price increases will range from $200 to $500. The financial firm expects the 512GB foldable iPhone will start at $2,399 and the 2TB model will go for $3,199.

"With NAND and DRAM costs rising sharply, we continue to expect Apple to raise the starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max by $200, with potentially larger increases at higher storage tiers," Woodring said. "Based on our memory cost forecasts for Apple, such pricing actions would allow Apple to maintain iPhone gross margins of ~40%, broadly in line with the FY21-FY25 average of 39.9%."

data.title: Anthropic IPO launch pushed toward mid-October: Reuters
data.description:
One of the world's most anticipated initial public offerings is facing a slight delay. Artificial intelligence company Anthropic (ANTHRO) is expected to start marketing its much-sought-after IPO in mid-October at the earliest, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The maker of the Claude chatbot is expected to complete the listing days before the U.S. midterm elections in November, according to the people who added that ⁠the plans, including the timing, could change.

Anthropic (ANTHRO), which was expected to make its IPO prospectus public as early as next week, marking the final stages of the listing, is now not expected to complete that step until late September, two of the people said.

The changes are not unusual, as companies frequently revise their IPO timelines depending on the market environment, regulatory feedback, and other conditions. Anthropic (ANTHRO) declined to respond to Reuters’ request for comments.

As part of the listing, the company is also planning to finalize a $15B revolving credit facility before meeting with analysts, including those at banks ‌financing the transaction, one of the people said.

The Financial Times reported on Friday that Morgan Stanley (MS) and Goldman Sachs (GS) are in talks with Anthropic (ANTHRO) to secure top roles in the offering, which is widely expected to value the company at more than $2T.

data.title: NFL preview: Sportsbooks take on the prediction market challenge; SCOTUS wildcard?
data.description:
The NFL season begins next week when the defending champion Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots on September 9. An equally intriguing match-up this season will be the sports betting sector versus the prediction market industry.

Sports betting is legal in some form in 39 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico, while 32 states have legalized online wagering. However, major markets such as California and Texas still do not allow conventional online sportsbooks, which opened the door for prediction markets such as Kalshi (KALSHI) and Polymarket (POLYMARKET) to gain a significant foothold, despite efforts by DraftKings (DKNG) and FanDuel (FLUT) to cut into the impact by introducing prediction market platforms of their own in some geographic markets.

Despite the new challenge from prediction markets, analysts expect sports betting revenue to top last year's tally of $30B for the NFL season, with the addition of Missouri to the sports betting mix helping to provide a boost. Notably, DraftKings (DKNG) and FanDuel (FLUT) are more promotional with sign-up incentives, reactivation offers, and profit boost offers than they were going into the week of the NFL last season. 

For the 2026–27 season, the NFL has renewed and expanded its official commercial relationship with sportsbooks. The league announced multiyear agreements with DraftKings (DKNG), FanDuel (FLUT), and Fanatics Betting and Gaming (FANA). DraftKings (DKNG) and FanDuel (FLUT) have held official NFL betting relationships since 2021, while Fanatics (FANA) joins the group under the new arrangement. The partnerships provide brand and marketing rights, but they also signal that the league continues to treat licensed sportsbooks as its primary commercial betting category.

For investors, licensed sportsbooks are still seen as a solid bet since they retain NFL partnerships, well-developed mobile products, brand clout, and responsible-gaming obligations. Prediction markets offer another route to NFL exposure, including in some states without online sportsbooks, but face numerous court cases and state-level enforcement uncertainty that could result in a Supreme Court showdown in 2027. If the prediction market industry survives the court challenges, the expectation is that Kalshi (KALSHI) and Polymarket (POLYMARKET) could become serious IPO candidates.

data.title: U.S. approves potential $5.75B in weapons sales to Saudi Arabia
data.description:
The U.S. State Department said ​Friday it ‌approved the potential sale of ​Joint Direct Attack ​Munitions-Extend Range to Saudi ⁠Arabia for ​an estimated $5B and a separate potential sale of AGT-1500 engines to Saudi Arabia ​for an ​estimated $750M (I, II).

Saudi Arabia has requested to purchase 5,000 KMU-572 Joint Direct Attack Munition guidance kits; 5,000 KMU-556 JDAM guidance kits; 5,000 BLU-111 500-lb general purpose bombs; 5,000 BLU-117 2,000-lb general purpose bombs; 60 AGT-1500 tank engines; and related equipment, the U.S. government said.

"The proposed sale will improve Saudi Arabia’s airborne defense capability to counter current and future regional threats, strengthen its homeland defense, and improve interoperability with systems operated by U.S. forces and other Gulf Region partners," the State Department said.

Boeing (BA) and Honeywell (HON) will be the principal contractors for the JDAM-ERs and AGT-150 engines, respectively.
